final.title: The quiet cost of overconfidence in a small business
final.body:
Overconfidence is often quiet because it hides inside a workflow that feels familiar. You keep doing the task by memory, so nobody stops to ask whether it is actually clean, fast, or safe. The cost shows up later as rework, missing approvals, duplicate entries, or a problem you only notice after it has moved downstream.

For an owner-operator, the question is not “use AI everywhere.” It is simpler: which single repeating workflow are you treating as fine without measuring its failure cost? If the task is manual, repeatable, and tied to a visible error mode, it is worth checking whether a small automation fits. If it is rare, sensitive, or depends on judgment, manual work may still be the better choice.

Bareni’s diagnostic is built around that kind of decision. The aim is to identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and define scope, measures, and limits before anything is built. Human approval stays mandatory for money movement and other high-risk decisions. That is not a loophole; it is the control.

Most founders only discover the quiet cost after they measure it.
